title: GitOps pipeline patterns for on-prem: TF modules, Helm upgrades, and image signing (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working draft for a repeatable GitOps CI/CD pattern we should recommend (and start implementing) for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Goal: reduce blast radius and make upgrades auditable while preserving the 'single source of truth' model (Git repos for infra + charts + app manifests). This doc mixes high-level patterns, concrete Terraform module notes, and an upgrade checklist for Argo/Helm/image signing workflows.

Context & constraints
- Target audience: infra owners and SREs supporting customer-private clusters (air-gapped or VPC-connected).
- Must support disconnected environments (image mirroring) and strict key control (KMS/HSM).
- Customers often want GitOps (Argo CD) + signed images + immutable releases. They also ask for infrastructure-as-code examples (Terraform modules) they can import.
- We operate with two main repo types: infra-terraform (state-backed remote) and gitops-manifests (kustomize/helm values + Argo apps).

High-level pattern summary
1) Source repos: 2 primary repos per customer deployment: infra-terraform (TF state in S3-like remote with encryption) and gitops-apps (Helm charts + value overlays + ArgoApp manifests).
2) CI pipeline (github actions / enterprise runner inside customer network): builds images, runs attestations, pushes to mirrored registry, generates a release manifest (image+chart+values) in a release branch.
3) Signing & attestation: CI produces cosign/notation attestation and stores a signed release bundle (SBOM + provenance) in an artifacts bucket accessible to Argo.
4) GitOps promotion: release branch (or tag) triggers an automated PR to gitops-apps that updates image tags and values; Argo CD detects and applies.
5) Upgrade safety net: Argo sync waves, canary strategies (traffic split + feature flag), and automated rollback via Argo Rollouts or built-in Helm hooks.

Notes on Terraform modules (practical, incremental)
- Module boundaries: keep networking (vpc, subnets, vpn), storage (object store/backups), and platform (argocd cluster role, node pools) separate. One module per responsibility simplifies upgrades.
- Interfaces: design modules with small, explicit input maps. Avoid opaque maps of maps; prefer typed inputs (list of objects where possible) so we can generate sane defaults in the customer wrapper repo.
- State backend: recommend encrypted object-store backend (S3 compatible) + Dynamo/consul-like lock. For on-prem, we default to Minio (with vault KMS) and Consul locks. Document the minimal setup in terraform-module/README.
- Secrets strategy: don't use TF for secret material whenever possible. Integrate with Vault/KMS via providers and reference rather than storing values in state. If customers insist on storing, mark sensitive and document lifecycle / rotation.
- Upgrade path for modules: keep a clear 'major-versioned' path (v1.x, v2.x) and a migration guide per major. For breaking changes, add a migration.tf snippet in the module root showing example replacements.
- Example module inputs (snippet, textual):
  - cluster_name (string)
  - argocd_admin_group (string)
  - image_registry_endpoint (string)
  - artifactory_mirror_enabled (bool)
  - remote_state_bucket (string)
  - kms_key_id (string)
  - enable_minio (bool)
- Recommended module outputs: argo_app_url, vault_address, remote_state_bucket, cluster_ca, worker_nodepool_ids. Keep outputs minimal and stable across versions.

Image signing + attestation flow (recommended pattern)
- CI build (local/runner inside customer network): build -> run unit/static tests -> produce image -> run cosign sign + produce provenance (in-toto / SLSA) -> push image+signature to mirror registry.
- Signing keys: prefer customer-managed KMS/HSM. Provide two options in our templates: cosign + KMS (recommended) OR offline keypair stored in sealed-secret for fully air-gapped setups. Document rotation steps.
- Attestation storage: bundle SBOM + provenance as a release artifact in object-store (same backend as TF remote-state or separate artifact bucket). Keep TTL and retention policy configurable.
- Verification at deploy time: Argo or an admission webhook should check cosign signatures against allowed key IDs and optionally require SBOM presence. For air-gapped clusters, provide a lightweight verifier sidecar or pre-sync job.

Argo + Helm upgrade mechanics (practical guidance)
- Argo structure: each logical service = one Argo Application manifest that points to a chart repo or to a path in gitops-apps. Keep chart values small and override only customer-specific items in overlay folders.
- Strategy for Helm charts: use chartmuseum or internal helm repo mirrored to customer. Charts are versioned; values files live in gitops-apps. Image tags are controlled via values files (avoid hardcoding in charts).
- Upgrade pattern (safe default):
  1) Build and push image -> create release branch with image tag and chart version bump.
  2) CI opens PR against gitops-apps (automated) updating values.yaml.
  3) Run an integration smoke pipeline against a pre-production namespace (ephemeral) via the same customer Argo instance (or a shadow cluster) to validate runtime.
  4) Merge PR to main triggers Argo sync in customer cluster. Use sync waves and hooks for ordering.
  5) Monitor for N minutes (configurable) and auto-promote or rollback. If using Argo Rollouts, rely on canary analysis metrics.
- Helm hooks: use pre-install and post-install hooks for migration jobs. Keep hooks idempotent and include timeouts. Document how to mark jobs as completed to avoid blocking rollouts.

Canary + rollback primitives
- Canary options: percent-based traffic split (requires service mesh / ingress support), or blue/green with DNS swap for simpler networks.
- Automated rollback triggers: failed liveness/readiness, error-rate spike, latency SLO breach, or custom metric thresholds from Prometheus.
- Rollback mechanics: prefer declarative Git rollback (revert the PR that updated the image tag) as the single source of truth. Argo will reconcile. For immediate rollback, Argo Rollouts can roll back faster but follow up with Git revert.

Checklist: pre-upgrade (team runbook)
- Ensure remote state backend healthy and lockable.
- Validate module version compatibility in a dry-run (terraform plan against staging workspace).
- Confirm image signatures and artifact bundle present in artifact store.
- Confirm Argo health: controller, repo-server, application-controller are green.
- Take backups: etcd snapshot, object-store snapshot of buckets, vault snapshot where applicable.
- Notify on-call and customer (if required) via Slack/email with rollout window.

Checklist: during upgrade
- Run terraform plan/apply with module version pinning. Monitor for drift and provider errors.
- CI should report: image push, signature creation, PR opened (link). Paste PR link in incident channel.
- Observe Argo sync progress; watch for stuck helm hooks, pending jobs. Use argo CLI to inspect logs if needed.

Checklist: post-upgrade
- Validate app hits readiness and smoke tests pass.
- Verify signature verification occurred (logs / admission webhook).
- Run post-deploy sanity checks (latency, error rates, token quotas).
- If all good, close release ticket and tag gitops-apps with release metadata.

Edge cases & operational notes
- Air-gapped: CI runs inside customer network. Provide an enterprise-runner image and a copy-playbook for mirroring registries and chart repos. Document a minimal 'bootstrap' flow that mirrors only required images for a single release if bandwidth is limited.
- Partial upgrades: when multiple components must be coordinated, use a release manifest that Argo applies in a single App-of-Apps pattern to preserve order.
- Secret rotation: rotation must be staged. Don't rotate KMS keys and Terraform remote-state keys simultaneously. Provide a rolling rotation recipe in module docs.

Open questions / TODOs
- Admission time signature verification: should Redwood provide a lightweight webhook for customers or recommend deploying cosign verification in-cluster? Tradeoffs: we can maintain a generic webhook but that increases support surface.
- Standardized release metadata spec: propose a simple JSON schema for release bundles (image, chart, values path, SBOM link, cosign key ID). Create a RFC.
- More module examples: add ready-to-use migration snippets for the most common breaking changes we see (argocd role changes, minio -> s3 switch).

Appendix: quick commands & snippets
- Cosign sign with KMS: cosign sign --key kms://gcp/projects/…/locations/…/keyRings/…/cryptoKeys/… <IMAGE>
- Verify: cosign verify --key kms://... <IMAGE>
- Terraform remote state example (text): backend "s3" { bucket = "customer-remote-state" key = "redwood/tfstate/cluster.tfstate" region = "us-west-2" encrypt = true }
- Argo manual sync: argocd app sync <app-name> --prune --timeout 300s

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic and customer-focused. Feedback requested: which parts add too much operator burden? Which flows should be fully automated vs documented?
- If we agree on the release bundle schema I can draft a minimal tool (release-bundle-generator) used by CI and consumed by Argo pre-sync hooks.

-- end of draft --
